## Packet part 7: OCTOBER15_REDESIGN_BACKEND_DELTA.md

Source: `docs/product/OCTOBER15_REDESIGN_BACKEND_DELTA.md`.

<!-- HALO-SOURCE-BEGIN docs/product/OCTOBER15_REDESIGN_BACKEND_DELTA.md -->
# HALO review redesign integration additions

This supplements the complete backend packet already given to Vibhav. The redesigned screens retain existing operation names, endpoints, ownership checks, revision reviews and unknown-outcome recovery. No API handlers or migrations are changed by this frontend pass.

Three optional response additions let the frontend represent the review's requested depth. Existing responses remain valid without them; missing evidence is never replaced by sample success.

## Opportunity venue dates

`CommunityOpportunity` supports `venueLocalDate`, `venueTimezone` and `venueTimezoneBasis`. See the exact types and validation in `lib/frontend/explore-opportunities.ts` and `lib/frontend/production/explore-service.ts`, plus `components/expanded/EXPLORE_BACKEND_DELTA.md`.

- Supply a genuine venue calendar date or a verified organizer/venue timezone. Do not use the user's home timezone as the event timezone.
- Instants must be valid, complete ISO timestamps. Impossible dates and an end before the start are rejected.
- Contradictory local dates and verified timezone conversions are rejected. Unknown or inferred context requires the user to choose a participation date.
- The conditions handoff carries the selected opportunity's date, meeting place and source into the existing outdoor planner. It requires acceptance and does not overwrite an edited draft silently. A meeting place remains distinct from an organization's office.
- Forecast requests use the accepted plan date/place. The server must resolve that place and return its actual coverage; no home forecast may be relabelled as the opportunity venue.
- Outdoor planning retains the existing 100-character coarse-place limit. A longer organizer address remains intact in its source context and requires explicit confirmation of a shorter planning area before a forecast request or save. It is never silently truncated.

## Reminder service evidence

The existing action snapshot may include `reminderStates`, keyed by canonical action ID. Each item contains:

```ts
type ReminderState = {
  actionRevision: number;
  scheduleSignature: string;
  status: 'pending' | 'registered' | 'scheduled' | 'delivered'
    | 'failed' | 'cancelled' | 'paused' | 'unknown';
  updatedAt: string;
  scheduledFor?: string;
  deliveredAt?: string;
  channel?: 'push' | 'email' | 'in-app';
};
```

Use the ordered signature in `lib/frontend/week-reminders.ts`:

```ts
JSON.stringify([
  action.date, meta.time, meta.zone, meta.reminder,
  meta.paused, meta.archived, action.state
])
```

These are server-owned read fields, not accepted client mutation evidence. The client requests reminders through existing task metadata and refreshes the existing action snapshot. A changed action revision or signature yields **Needs sync**, not a scheduled-success badge. Scheduled and delivered states require their respective timestamps. Device permission alone is not scheduling, delivery or reading.

Return the same evidence after mutation receipts and reloads when available. Service jobs must still enforce quiet hours, timezone/DST, idempotency, cancellation, device ownership and provider failures as specified in the complete packet. Turning a task off or completing it must cancel or pause its service job; an unconfirmed stop remains visible. Unknown states must be reconciled, not retried as a new job.

The existing repeating-plan requests, source-follow drafts and preparation checklists are not silently promoted to durable backend features by this redesign. Their persistence and automation remain the corresponding requirements in the full packet. See `components/expanded/HOMEPAGE_BACKEND_DELTA.md` for precise client state and refresh behavior.

## Luna source findings and interpretation

Existing `LunaMessage.text`, `sources`, navigation and proposals are retained. Assistant messages may additionally include:

```ts
type LunaEvidenceBlock = {
  kind: 'fact' | 'interpretation' | 'next-step';
  text: string;
  sourceIndexes: number[];
  scope?: string;
  observedAt?: string;
};
```

`evidence` is an array of these blocks. Indexes refer only to the current message's `sources` array. Fact blocks require at least one valid source reference; indexes must be unique integers within the array. Dates must be valid explicit-zone ISO timestamps. The validator rejects unsupported block kinds, malformed content, user-authored evidence blocks and unsafe source URLs.

The renderer labels source findings, Luna's interpretation and suggested next steps separately. Legacy text still displays, but an unlinked source list is not presented as claim-level grounding. Optional `scope` should carry applicability limits such as outdoor monitor versus indoor measurement; `observedAt` is the source observation/publication time, not the retrieval time.

The server must actually retrieve and verify those references. A `fact` label supplied by a model is not verification. Source retrieval must preserve dates, units, missingness, geographic scope and consent. Source content remains data, not tool instructions. No evidence block can execute an action: all changes still use the existing exact proposal revision, expiry, confirmation, stable operation ID and receipt workflow.

## Deployment and acceptance

### October 16 optional color preference

The existing settings snapshot and display-group save accept `display.palette?: 'ocean' | 'forest' | 'iris'`. This is independent of `appearance: 'system' | 'light' | 'dark'`. Persist and return the accepted palette in the canonical settings receipt and subsequent reads. Omission remains valid and falls back to Ocean; unsupported values are rejected. The frontend does not claim the selected palette was saved when a legacy receipt omits it, and explains that the default was retained. Unsaved choices stay drafts; Cancel, retained drafts, conflict rebase, unknown-outcome recovery and explicit Save remain unchanged. The selected private export includes the saved palette, not an unconfirmed draft. No new endpoint or provider is needed.

Language preferences remain compatible with existing `en` / `es` values, but Spanish is explicitly marked Coming soon. A preference is not a claim that the app has been translated. Color palettes do not change risk thresholds, scientific factor colors or score values.

The public homepage accepts an optional `HALO_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` HTTPS origin for canonical metadata. Configure it only after the deployed domain is verified. Private app routes remain noindex. The isolated review Site is not the production app origin and does not connect to backend services.

Before release, run the connected concern-to-result workflow, project generation, venue lookup/forecast, grounded Luna actions and reminder lifecycle using disposable accounts. Verify real persistence, access isolation, provider errors and retry recovery. Frontend contract tests use controlled responses and do not prove those services are deployed. Full reviewed Spanish and physical-device/screen-reader acceptance remain separate release decisions.

## Packet part 8: OCTOBER16_REDESIGN_IMPLEMENTATION.md

Source: `docs/continuation/OCTOBER16_REDESIGN_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

<!-- HALO-SOURCE-BEGIN docs/continuation/OCTOBER16_REDESIGN_IMPLEMENTATION.md -->
# October 16 frontend redesign implementation and verification

This pass responds to the user's request for a visibly substantive redesign following the 19-page Congressional App Challenge review. Homeguard now starts with the user's work, My Week is a continuous calendar and agenda, and Explore has clearer activity, project and map destinations. The pass also adds compatible frontend support for reminder service evidence, source-linked Luna answers and opportunity venue dates. The redesigned public review is published as version 53.

The earlier [PDF requirement verification](OCTOBER15_PDF_REQUIREMENT_VERIFICATION.md) remains the historical record of what was incomplete. This receipt records subsequent implementation, not a claim that the entire connected product is finished. Final browser regressions and release acceptance are recorded separately below.

## Scope and preservation

The existing HALO identity, light and dark themes, source qualifications and feature inventory remain the baseline. The responsive shell from the preceding revision is retained: compact phone navigation, constrained tablet surfaces and a collapsible desktop sidebar. This pass changes the composition within that shell, rather than stretching a phone design or merely renaming headings.

The [complete backend handoff](../product/HALO_COMPLETE_BACKEND_HANDOFF.md) already supplied to Vibhav and the [frontend integration contract](FRONTEND_INTEGRATION_READY.md) remain authoritative. No backend API handler, endpoint, database migration, scoring formula or operation registry is changed by this pass. Three optional response additions are documented below. No backend branch was merged and no message was sent to Vibhav.

The 45-feature inventory is retained. Existing record ownership, exact revision-bound mutation reviews, unknown-outcome reconciliation, private attachment review, current-home separation and source provenance must continue to pass their integration tests. Preserving the inventory is not proof of every possible user, device and service combination.

## Substantive screen changes

### Today and Homeguard

- Today uses a compact environmental briefing with a restrained landscape, concise score and grouped factor readings. The large decorative overview dial no longer dominates the working page. Factor details, sources, household guidance and score-method explanations remain accessible.
- Homeguard puts the household workspace and exact current-record continuation before the environmental overview on phones. Desktop separates the workbench from environmental context instead of presenting equal oversized cards.
- Tests, Home care, Food and Garden, and Summary remain accessible. Creation actions, recent records and factual recorded stages are retained without repeating an Open action on every row.
- Test creation groups the sample/context fields separately from timing/provider details. Original report results, amendments, comparisons, archive handling and My Week follow-up retain their existing data model.
- Maintenance separates routines from observations. A discoverable **Record suspected mold** entry uses the existing Other observation type, preserves an existing draft and does not invent a mold diagnosis, new test enum or indoor measurement.
- Homeguard now evaluates test, home-care and food/garden availability independently. An unavailable collection does not hide other loaded records or display false zero counts; the two controlled production availability cases passed.

Primary sources: `components/foundation/PersonalHero.tsx`, `environment-briefing.css`, `components/expanded/HomeOverviewWorkspace.tsx`, `home-workbench.css`, `components/homeguard/TestsWorkspace.tsx`, `MaintenanceWorkspace.tsx`, and `home-record-workflows.css`.

### My Week

- A compact current-day masthead and one Add task action lead the page. The five original environmental scenes remain in a smaller landscape window with accessible pause and next controls; scene rotation and reduced-motion behavior remain available.
- The calendar, search/filter controls and selected agenda form one continuous working surface. Week, Month and Agenda retain their distinct behavior.
- Desktop has an In focus support column for the next action, attention, preparation, upcoming work and supporting tools. On phones, the calendar and selected agenda precede those tools. Calendar setup and automation intent are disclosed rather than repeated as equally prominent cards.
- Task creation, editing, scheduling, completion/reopening, pauses, archives, deletions, saved-for-later, manual recurrence, effort planning, exports, Journal, Patterns, recap, connected records and outdoor planning remain reachable.
- Loading and unavailable action data do not appear as a successfully empty calendar. The Add task action is disabled when its required action data is unavailable.
- Timed task dates and clocks now use the same display-zone conversion in the calendar, selected agenda, next action and upcoming rail. All-day dates remain calendar dates. Saved source timezone and editor values are not rewritten for display.

Primary sources: `components/expanded/MyWeekWorkspace.tsx`, `HomepageHub.tsx`, `WeekPlanningRail.tsx`, `WeekOutdoors.tsx`, `week-command-center.css`, and `lib/frontend/week-timeline.ts`.

### Explore

- Projects, Get involved and the map have separate, balanced destinations with regular rectangular contextual imagery and shorter action-oriented copy. The map remains a preview opening its full specialist view.
- Project setup no longer presents several competing generation/preference controls together. Project guides gain a step outline and focused current-step workspace while preserving materials, instructions, checkpoints, safety, source and canonical step continuity.
- Opportunity details separate essential time/place information, the actual work, preparation and the organizer's next step. Source freshness, suitability, cancellation and participation qualifications remain.
- The selected opportunity can prepare an outdoor-conditions draft with its date, meeting place and source. The user must choose **Use opportunity details** or **Keep current plan**. An existing edited plan is not silently replaced, and no forecast request is made while that choice is pending.
- Venue dates are derived only from supplied venue-local dates or source-backed venue timezones. Missing authoritative date context requires a deliberate date selection; the user's home timezone is not treated as the venue timezone.

Primary sources: `components/expanded/ExploreWorkspace.tsx`, `ExploreProjects.tsx`, `ExploreOpportunities.tsx`, `explore-refinement.css`, and `lib/frontend/explore-opportunities.ts`.

### Settings and shared presentation

- Settings gains a section navigator alongside the active panel on wide layouts, with active-section and unsaved-draft indicators. Group-scoped save/cancel, conflict handling, retained drafts and Back/Forward remain.
- Notification settings link directly to the reminder manager. Device registration, a reminder request, scheduling, delivery and reading remain distinct states.
- Shared spacing, radius and shadow tokens are now consumed by the new workspaces and controls. This is adoption in the redesigned surfaces, not a claim that every older style literal has been removed.
- Random floating particles are removed from environmental scenes. Page-wide decorative atmosphere is reduced; contextual scene layers and meaningful transitions remain. Device reduced motion is authoritative even when a review URL requests full motion.
- Public canonical metadata can use a validated `HALO_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`. It must be configured only for a verified production domain. Private application routes remain noindex.

Primary sources: `components/expanded/SettingsWorkspace.tsx`, `SettingsPanels.tsx`, `settings-refinement.css`, `interface-refinement.css`, `components/foundation/EnvironmentalScene.tsx`, `SceneExperience.tsx`, `app/page.tsx`, and `lib/frontend/public-origin.ts`.

### Follow up corrections

The full runs found real navigation defects as well as outdated test expectations. These corrections are implemented and rechecked:

- Notes capture navigation before an awaited save, including same-origin main-tab links and history changes. A late success cannot redirect the user away from their newer destination. A confirmed save clears only its exact submitted draft and context snapshots; newer edits survive. The final production test verifies one canonical write, the intended Today destination and an empty new-note form on return.
- Settings section switching retains only its own history marker, never copies Next's internal history state. Switching sections, returning to the section list and directly opened panels are covered by passing release and static-preview checks.
- Opportunity addresses remain complete. When the existing outdoor planning area's 100-character contract cannot hold the full address, the user must explicitly shorten and confirm a planning area before requesting conditions or saving that plan. The source meeting address remains available; it is not silently truncated or represented as a verified forecast location.
- Homeguard's first-viewport priority and overview groups now register independently with the reveal system. The tall parent remains stationary and controls are not nested inside competing animations. All 16 final motion checks pass, including below-fold and device-reduced-motion behavior.

## Backend compatible additions

The exact contract is in [HALO review redesign integration additions](../product/OCTOBER15_REDESIGN_BACKEND_DELTA.md). These are three optional response groups, not three new endpoints. Legacy responses remain accepted without fabricated success.

| Response group | Frontend behavior | Backend acceptance still required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opportunity `venueLocalDate`, `venueTimezone` and `venueTimezoneBasis` | Rejects invalid instants and contradictory authoritative dates; preserves a source-backed venue date in participation and the reviewed outdoor handoff. Unknown dates remain unset. | Organizer/venue location resolution, timezone authority, freshness and forecasts for the accepted meeting place. |
| Action snapshot `reminderStates`, keyed by canonical action ID | Shows pending, registered, scheduled, delivered, failed, cancelled, paused and unknown service states. Requires valid timestamps and exact action revision/schedule binding. A changed binding shows Needs sync. Older snapshots show an unconfirmed request. | Real scheduling, quiet hours, timezone/DST behavior, cancellation, provider delivery, device ownership and canonical status reconciliation. |
| Assistant message `evidence` blocks | Separates From the source, Luna's interpretation and Suggested next step. Validates referenced source indexes, block kinds and dated scope. Legacy text/source lists remain visibly unqualified at statement level. | Genuine retrieval, source verification, accurate scope and timestamps, model grounding, consent and provider/tool behavior. |

Reminder evidence is server-owned read data, not accepted client mutation evidence. Refresh rereads the existing action snapshot; it does not resend a notification or create a job. Completion or disabling a task does not claim cancellation until the service confirms it. Delivered does not mean read. Manual Prepare next occurrence remains manual.

Preparation checklists, automatic-repeat intent and source-follow drafts retain their explicit visit-local status until their previously specified services are connected. This redesign does not silently promote them to durable saves.

The forecast contract still needs an explicit decision on whether `horizonStart` and `horizonEnd` are inclusive venue-local dates or timestamp boundaries. Their existing string types do not settle timezone or boundary semantics. The current date-prefix horizon comparison is not verified source coverage. Resolve this with near-midnight and DST cases before connected acceptance; see [homepage backend delta](../../components/expanded/HOMEPAGE_BACKEND_DELTA.md).

Chart SVG identity and large-calendar checks cover particular unnecessary reconstruction paths, not exhaustive React profiling.

Final controlled measurements: the 500-task view became visible in 1,983 ms and filtered in 181 ms (CLS 0.0158). # HALO homepage integration delta

## October 16 review redesign: canonical reminder status

The calendar-first frontend now accepts an optional, read-only `reminderStates` map in the existing `ActionSnapshot`. No endpoint, mutation command, preference field or scheduler was added. Existing responses without this field remain valid and display a requested reminder without claiming scheduling or delivery.

Each map key is a canonical action ID. Its value is the `ReminderState` type in `lib/frontend/week-reminders.ts`:

```ts
{
  actionRevision: number;
  scheduleSignature: string;
  status: 'pending' | 'registered' | 'scheduled' | 'delivered'
    | 'failed' | 'cancelled' | 'paused' | 'unknown';
  updatedAt: string;
  scheduledFor?: string;
  deliveredAt?: string;
  channel?: 'push' | 'email' | 'in-app';
}
```

The signature is `JSON.stringify([action.date, meta.time, meta.zone, meta.reminder, meta.paused, meta.archived, action.state])`. It excludes private preparation and history. Return the exact action revision and signature against which the scheduler state was established. Older evidence is retained as history but displayed as **Needs sync**, never as a current Scheduled or Delivered state. `updatedAt`, `scheduledFor` and `deliveredAt` must be valid instants with an explicit timezone. Scheduled requires `scheduledFor`; delivered requires `deliveredAt`. Unknown actions or malformed entries invalidate the snapshot rather than allowing unverified success labels.

Task preference edits continue through the existing revision-bound action command. Reminder evidence is not a writable preference or task metadata field. The service must independently enforce ownership, scheduling consent, quiet hours, timezone/DST, cancellation for completed/paused/archived tasks, idempotency and delivery receipts, as required by the original whole-app handoff. The UI's Refresh reminder status performs the existing action snapshot read, not a retry/send job. A delivered receipt does not assert that the message was read. A disabled request without a canonical cancelled/paused receipt does not claim that a job has stopped.

My Week now has a single continuous calendar/search/agenda surface, a compact masthead with the original optional landscape controls, and a distinct supporting rail. All earlier task sheets, captured-review actions, private preparation, manual recurrence, actual-date recap, Journal, Patterns, season, exports and linked record dates remain. Preparation checks and automatic-repeat choices retain their explicit visit-only scope. This redesign does not claim those services have become durable.

The opportunity-to-outdoors bridge uses a visit-local, explicitly accepted handoff from Explore. It does not transmit a place or date in the URL, fetch a forecast before acceptance, silently overwrite an outdoor draft, register participation or move an organizer event. The accepted source-local date and place feed the existing forecast read; absent venue-local date stays blank until the user deliberately supplies one. The optional event timezone fields are documented in `EXPLORE_BACKEND_DELTA.md`.

Timed task summaries and Up next now use the same display-zone day and clock as the calendar. Saved source-zone schedules, immutable dates and ICS export remain unchanged. Forecast horizon acceptance is still a specific integration gate: the current `ForecastSnapshot` declares `horizonStart`/`horizonEnd` only as strings, without specifying whether they are local inclusive calendar dates or absolute interval boundaries. Vibhav must choose and document that representation, including timezone and endpoint inclusivity, and test near-midnight/DST boundaries. Per-period start/end already require explicit timezone instants. Do not treat the existing horizon label or its date-prefix comparison as verified source coverage until that contract is settled.

October12, 2026. Yogi requested My Week as the first tab and default homepage, followed by Today, Homeguard and Explore. This is a wireframe extension, not authorization to change Vibhav's backend or bypass approval. The shared navigation order is updated, but production delivery flags and current live entry gates remain. The expanded static review opens My Week by default; explicit tab, factor, record and specialist-map links retain their owner.

## Verified current boundary

The current repository has `/api/daily-score`, `/api/home-guard`, Journal/history and notification/push foundations, but no owned Plan/action/recurrence/aggregate homepage service. The existing notification preference route edits alert-type preferences, not scheduled task-reminder jobs. StageRuntime can provide authoritative overview scores, including unavailable data; the hosted review instead uses the original shared design-fixture selector. All new private homepage records remain in the visit-local HomeWorkspaceState. No provider call, registration, email, notification delivery or account mutation was added.

## Proposed contracts, not existing endpoints

- Authenticated aggregate reads: owned canonical actions/metadata, selected owned home and community records, actual evidence changes and authoritative empty/loading/stale/error states. Preserve stable IDs, source/context versions and source dates. Historical observations, report timestamps and inventory items do not become unsolicited tasks. A homepage is not permission to read every free-text note into Luna.
- Attention: join earlier chosen plans, waiting actions/cases, independently expected result dates, actually entered unreviewed reports and precisely linked source changes. Deduplicate source revisions and acknowledgement. An expected lab date is not guaranteed delivery or an emergency deadline; viewing/acknowledging is not task completion. A cancellation retains the plan and invites explicit review, never silent deletion or rescheduling.
- Recorded progress: authoritative completion events/timestamps with user/display timezone and audit history. Summaries use when actions were completed, not their original due dates. Project steps are a subset of action totals. Archived completed history stays available. Unknown completion dates remain excluded and identified. No inferred health improvement, hazard remediation, pollution reduction or energy/water savings.
- Participation: add an explicit actual `participatedOn` calendar date distinct from chosen activity date and status-update date. Existing hours remain validated, self-reported and optional. Legacy undated participation is retained but not assigned to a week. Actual date corrections/history need captured revision and reconciliation. Reporting attendance is not organizer verification; meeting places stay distinct from offices and mailing addresses.
- Preparation: owned checklist checks bound to an exact action/origin revision and schedule/evidence signature. Changing relevant instructions, dates or source versions invalidates a prior ready-looking state. Preserve failed/offline drafts, recheck revision at Save and never update registration, attendance, action completion or source instructions as a side effect. The wireframe records what the user checked, not a safety certificate. External Maps searches disclose the saved place label and do not transmit a home address or request GPS automatically.
- Recurrence: durable owned series/preferences, explicit fixed-calendar versus after-completion rules, supported all-day/timed semantics, timezone/DST/end/skip/pause/cancel scopes and idempotent occurrence materialization. Requesting automatic next occurrences is consent intent, not an active scheduler. Wireframe dates are previews only; current manual Prepare next remains. Jobs must not duplicate canonical occurrences, overwrite user edits or erase completed history, including after partial/unknown outcomes and repeated retries. Preference changes require current series/context revision and an exact affected scope.
- Reminders: durable consented intent, authoritative channel/browser capability and delivery state, quiet hours/timezone, pending/scheduled/cancelled/failed receipts and retry/reconciliation. Paused/completed/archived items do not continue producing task reminders. Existing global alert preferences are not equivalent to these new action intents; separate inbox/push/email controls need additive reviewed contracts. Browser permission is not delivery confirmation. No scheduler or push reliability claim is established by the UI.
- Luna: authorized minimal aggregate read tools for explicit attention/recap requests, and existing captured-scope confirmed action tools. The new deterministic replies use saved-task metadata and completion counts, not private Journal or preparation text. Production should expose typed capability/error/provider state, context/revision checks, current owned aggregate facts and exact confirmation for proposed mutations. No account-wide context or arbitrary tool authority follows from placing Luna on a homepage.
- Production entry: once this screen is approved and implemented, authentication/onboarding entry can target the delivered `/plan` homepage. Preserve existing `/today`, `/home`, `/act` and all specialist/deep links. Do not make an undelivered route the live default merely because the wireframe opens there. Optional device recovery, export, deletion and account/context changes must cover all new records/preferences/jobs.

The full existing My Week, Explore, food, privacy and whole-app handoff contracts still apply. Vibhav retains backend ownership. This delta is saved for the deferred handoff, not sent to him and not proof of production readiness.

# Explore evergreen workspace and integration delta

## October 16 review completion: venue dates and conditions handoff

No endpoint, migration, backend operation or scoring formula is changed. The existing `opportunities.search` response accepts three optional additive fields on an opportunity: `venueLocalDate` (valid source-supplied `YYYY-MM-DD`), `venueTimezone` (valid IANA zone), and `venueTimezoneBasis` (`source` or `inferred`). Old responses remain valid. Only an explicit source-supplied date or a zone marked `source` may prefill a participation calendar date. Missing, inferred or conflicting context never falls back to the user's home, browser zone or a UTC string slice. A conflicting explicit date and source-zone date is rejected. Vibhav can supply these fields within the already-required scheduled-time/source-timezone contract; the client does not infer authoritative venue geography.

The opportunity's Check outdoor conditions action prepares a visit-local `week:outdoor-handoff` for the existing outdoor planner. It contains the opportunity ID/title, source-derived date (or an empty date), organizer place/address, source URL/check date and any source-backed zone/start instant. This is not a forecast, registration or new canonical schedule. The planner asks before applying it, retains active drafts and uses the existing forecast service only after the user chooses the date/place. No precise home location or private note enters a navigation URL. Unknown dates and rolling programs require deliberate date selection. Existing forecast horizon, per-factor availability, no-safety-guarantee and revision-bound save protections remain authoritative.

Explore now uses three clear hub destinations, one project-interest composer, result-only refresh/filter tools, photo-led project results and a step-outline/current-step workspace. Every prior generation, guide/version, selected-step plan, pause/progress/history, note, outreach, organization and source route remains. Activity photography is contextual, never a claimed event venue or measured build diagram.

The user explicitly restores scheduled-opportunity discovery alongside rolling programs, inside an evergreen three-path hub. The earlier statement that no event service is needed is superseded for this finder. This is additional backend scope, not authorization to implement production routes from the frontend lane.

### Interest-to-project service

Return a validated semantic visual family with each project, plus optional reviewed image/diagram references and rights/provenance. The frontend should render an appropriate activity-specific sketch or legitimate illustration rather than treating every generated topic as gardening. Decorative art must not look like a measured construction plan or evidence of a real venue. Unknown families need an honest neutral fallback.

Return fewer with a clear reason when source-backed fits are exhausted; do not fill a requested count with irrelevant projects. Preserve started projects and source/template versions. Unknown interests mean unavailable reviewed support, not proof that no such project exists on the web. Keep a cancellable request handle, retry identity, context/preference version, response validation and latest-request commit rules. A cancelled or stale reply cannot replace newer Luna/Explore ideas. Retain current results and editable input on failure; preserve shared generation state and canonical saved actions across views. The review animation represents a 1.2-second simulated preparation, not real searching. Existing `/api/assistant` still lacks these contracts.

Resolve a user-selected city/county/ZIP through a real provider with ambiguous/unsupported/failed outcomes. Area changes invalidate old query scope and nearby results while retaining privately saved commitments. Do not send household evidence, private notes or other unrelated fields to the discovery provider.

Full/cancelled/postponed/date-changed/expired states remain distinct. Only sessions starting in the future or eligible rolling programs enter the primary finder. Content rights and image provenance are reviewed; a venue photograph is not invented from generic nature art.

Curated official pages, organizer feeds and approved structured listings can form a bounded acquisition service. Registry/link verification is separate from human verification and partnership. Updates need source-specific freshness, cancellation/expiry checks, caching, retry/rate limits and a last-successful-fetch ledger. 1. Load authorized dated Today/Homeguard evidence server-side. Preserve source, metric, units, observation/retrieval date, geographic basis, age, provenance, missing/error state and owner-record revision. The target is 10 to 15; return fewer plus useful refinement when insufficient safe fits exist, rather than fabricating sources or unsafe filler.

Record the query/source/content version and review status. General interest ideas must not masquerade as evidence-driven recommendations.
4. Return stable batch/idea IDs, eligibility reasons, evidence references, why-this-idea, time/material ranges, instructions, constraints, maintenance, completion criteria and sources. Model output is schema-validated and source-checked. Regional radon/utility samples are not property readings; dated AQI/UV/weather never promises a safe current outdoor window. Planting or composting does not establish reduced PFAS exposure or repair a hazardous home. No new risk/benefit score or estimated environmental result is inferred.

Started projects retain their original template/source versions, edited task titles/dates/status and notes; regeneration must not mutate existing work. Provide an authenticated capability registry and owner-scoped conversation/messages. Distinguish explanations, safe screen navigation, record lookup, reversible proposed writes and consequential external actions. Read only the authorized minimal context needed for the request. ## Product boundary

Explore is an evergreen community hub, not a live event calendar or news feed. Its map, volunteering finder, community guide, organization directory, reviewed project paths, private notes and outreach entry points do not depend on a featured current event. Actual events can be discovered on official organizer sites. No event import, ongoing calendar ingestion or cancellation-monitoring service is required for this initial version. Earlier A03 catalogue/participation requirements remain a possible later capability, not an enabled service in this revised design.

Official resource guides and learning/project content can be bundled, versioned and reviewed periodically. Evergreen does not mean permanent factual accuracy: links, contact roles, instructions and service coverage still need review. Live map evidence keeps its own dated source/update rules; this request does not make measurements static. Organization records use the existing directory foundation after its coverage and error semantics are verified.

## Suggested contact-resolution contract

Use an issue category, recipient class, explicit user area choice and optional confirmed provider/organization/district ID. Return a small candidate set with stable ID/revision, official organization/office, public role/name only if published, responsibility, service jurisdiction, supported topics, public email or official form URL, source URL, checked date and human verification state. A working URL is not human verification.

Distinguish candidate matches, ambiguous jurisdiction, additional location information needed, no public email, no reviewed coverage, stale contact and failed lookup. Explain why each candidate fits. Prioritize the responsible office/role, not an invented personal contact. Do not claim every office publishes an email address. Offer an official-form/copy-message fallback.

A water utility requires a confirmed provider or service-area match; ZIP/county alone may be ambiguous. A representative may require reviewed district boundaries and more precise user input. If exact location is necessary, ask separately, explain the destination/use and avoid routine storage. A private landlord is manually supplied by the user, not discovered from their location. Changing topic, area, provider or recipient invalidates the prior suitability confirmation.

Suggested API groups, not existing endpoints: public contact resolution/detail; owned outreach drafts with selected evidence/note revision snapshots; private email connection/revocation; explicit confirmed send attempts and attempt-status reconciliation. Reuse HALO's session/owner/idempotency transport, not a second identity system.

## Notes and Luna contract

Preserve original text and revision history. A general question or idea is not a measured observation. Each selected note is loaded and authorized server-side; client-provided text is untrusted data, never tool instructions. Default context excludes place/date and all unrelated records. The final request shows exactly which text is included, its source/revision and what the provider may retain. Free-text Journal context remains excluded by default; this proposal applies only to deliberately selected Explore notes.

Luna may help clarify a question, organize a factual observation or suggest a follow-up, with uncertainty and citations where needed. It must not diagnose a contaminant from a note, claim an observation is a verified measurement, quietly overwrite a note, email someone or submit an official report. Proposed note edits/actions require a separate preview and confirmation. Do not use the existing assistant endpoint's page/question fields as proof of a secure selected-record workflow.

Contact/outreach inclusion is separate from Luna consent. A chosen note adds only its title and description; its text may itself be sensitive, so always review it. Keep per-recipient snapshots. Changed or deleted notes require deliberate reselection before sending; they never silently rewrite an edited message. Previously exported/copied text cannot be recalled by deleting the source note.

## Email feasibility and safety

Sending from the app is feasible using the [Gmail messages.send API](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.messages/send) and [MIME message workflow](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/sending). The recipient can use any email domain. HALO would send from the user's connected account, not from the developer's connected Gmail or a shared application identity.

Request only [`gmail.send`](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/auth/scopes), a sensitive scope requiring Google's applicable verification. It does not authorize reading an inbox or replies. Ask at the moment the user chooses email sending, not during onboarding. Use the [web-server OAuth flow](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server), secure state/redirect handling, encrypted token storage, revocation/disconnect and reliable account ownership. Never put tokens in frontend assets, URLs, logs or the static review archive.

Validate exact recipients, subject/header injection, body bounds, allowed attachments and connection identity server-side. Revalidate contact and selected-note revisions at confirmation. Bind confirmation to an immutable message snapshot and a stable operation ID. Serialize submission, prevent double-click/retry duplicates, rate-limit and provide abuse safeguards. Do not queue or retry a message without an explicit user decision.

The [Gmail error guide](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/handle-errors) warns that API success is not proof of successful mail delivery. Use separate prepared/submitting/submitted/failed/unknown states, never Delivered or Replied from a send response. For an ambiguous timeout, reconcile the durable attempt before offering another send. Send-only access may not allow the backend to inspect Sent mail; where it cannot conclusively resolve the attempt, retain Unknown and offer a user check in Gmail rather than expanding inbox permissions silently. A sample 'no submission recorded' outcome is a wireframe branch, not proof that every production timeout is safely retryable.

Replies and provider delivery/bounce tracking are separate future contracts. Follow-up reminders do not send follow-up mail automatically. Review [Google Workspace user-data policy](https://developers.google.com/workspace/workspace-api-user-data-developer-policy) before any later Gmail/Luna data processing; connecting sending does not grant general mailbox access.

## Official resources checked for this review

- [National Park Service volunteering](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/volunteer/become.htm): official directions to location/activity searches and park volunteer pages. HALO links this guide because the dynamic Volunteer.gov page did not render fully in the source check.
- [U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service participation](https://www.fws.gov/get-involved): official ways to get involved. Availability belongs to the organizer, not HALO.
- [North Carolina Stream Watch](https://www.deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/water-resources/water-resources-public-information/water-education-programs/water-education-and-outreach/nc-stream-watch): state-specific learning/participation; some shared observations can be public. No submission API is implied.
- [USAGov elected-official directory](https://www.usa.gov/elected-officials): federal/state/local contact routes, not guaranteed personal email discovery.
- [EPA contact routing](https://www.epa.gov/aboutepa/forms/contact-epa) and [water quality report resources](https://www.epa.gov/ccr): official starting points, not automatic local-office matching or emergency handling.

## Review and release gates

Test the exact selected context, per-recipient drafts, contact reconfirmation, stale-note blocking, save/conflict/offline retention, delete scope, official-link handoff without private URL fields, Gmail cancel/failed/unknown/duplicate/reconciliation branches, regular image geometry/failure, keyboard/disclosures and light/dark narrow/enlarged layouts. Approved archives remain immutable. Physical Safari, screen-reader end-to-end behavior, translations, live resolver/record permissions, provider consent and actual sending require later verification before release.

## Later October 10 active-outcome extension

The new frontend goes from discovery to preparation, deliberate action and review. It can now demonstrate private volunteering commitments, ongoing project workspaces, topic/group/note/outreach result records, canonical shared task bundles and public map references attached to notes. These still use the existing isolated memory providers. No new authenticated route, schema, email delivery or selected-note AI service was built.

### Required owned records

- Personal volunteering commitments: chosen opportunity title/organizer, cause, optional reviewed public HTTPS URL, private place label, planned date, preparation/access notes, dated self-reported state, optional nonnegative hours, factual activity/result, user-supplied organizer reference, follow-up date and immutable update history. This is private user-entered content, not a public event catalogue. Store source verification separately from the user's confirmation. A participation report needs an actual date and factual activity; future planned dates cannot become future attendance claims.
- Project workspaces: template ID/version, reviewed suitability/prerequisites/materials, owner, active/paused/completed status, goal, chosen step references, private notes, recorded result and review history. Steps reference the SAME shared action IDs as My Week. The preview's deterministic step keys are not a production template-version contract. Preserve user-edited action titles/schedules/status on repeated selection. A reopened step makes an earlier completion snapshot need review; no auto-completion or benefit estimate.
- Follow-through cases: stable owner-scoped ID tied to a community topic, organization, note or outreach request; desired answer/result; own status/date; factual result; optional genuine user-supplied reference; next step/check-back date; canonical related action ID; original update history. A user's status is not agency verification, laboratory evidence or an organizer receipt. Distinguish closure without a result from an answered question.
- Note/public-evidence references: stable record ID, layer/evidence kind, original observation date, geographic basis/scope, source/revision/rights and snapshot metadata loaded and authorized server-side. The current fixture retains only title, record ID, date and scope. Never include the home pin through the public-map pathway. Add a selected reference only after an explicit user action, preserve existing writing, and preview it independently for Luna or exports.

### Atomicity, ownership and task relationships

Bundle confirmation creates only deliberately selected tasks. Implement an idempotent atomic operation, with unique owner/template-version/step/occurrence keys and canonical parent/child IDs. Return existing duplicate matches rather than resetting them. A failed bundle must create no partial work; an unknown write requires reconciliation. A sample synchronous add is not proof of backend atomicity.

Follow-up tasks remain separate from their source record. Deleting a note removes its OWN case/history and unsaved case drafts in one authorized transaction; independent My Week tasks, other records and already copied outreach text remain. Return linked-record scope before confirmation. Account export/deletion/recovery must cover new commitments, cases, project notes, histories and reminder jobs. No private record can be loaded by an unauthenticated public map or another household.

Project completion uses actual owned step states and a factual recorded result, not a carousel view or a percentage animation. Pause/resume must define its relationship to existing task schedules/reminders without silently deleting them. The current preview pauses editing in the project workspace but retains independent My Week tasks. Production needs reviewed server transition rules and revision-conflict handling across both consumers.

### Separate action outputs from environmental outcomes

Action evidence includes user-reported hours, contacted/participated status and completed steps. Tangible outputs include a received dated report, a chosen qualified test, a reply or an actual reference. Environmental outcomes need compatible dated measurements or official confirmation. Never convert completed tasks, volunteering hours, reports sent or proximity into pollution removed, water-quality improvement, health benefit or causal attribution. The frontend explains how each action can support awareness, qualified decisions or community stewardship without claiming success before evidence exists.

### Source and release status

The local `/api/volunteer` directory exists, including its documented successful-empty database-error fallback. The local tree still has no implemented owned commitments/project/case/bulk-action endpoints. No remote backend deployment was audited in this refinement. Vibhav must implement or verify the required contracts, flags, privacy/retention, source coverage, transport and production permissions before wiring the approved frontend. Existing map geography/fixtures are reused; no live source, scoring formula, provider key, registration, message or agency API was added.

## October 11 connected guidance and assistant tools

### Real programmes and practical guides

The review bundles official-source guides for Keep Charlotte Beautiful, Catawba Riverkeeper, TreesCharlotte, Mecklenburg community gardens and Union County Extension. Exact recognized NC place names select reviewed resource coverage; arbitrary labels do not create nearby results. `/api/volunteer` currently accepts authenticated county/cause queries and returns directory fields, not programme requirements/instructions, typed addresses, events or a geospatial finder. Its HTTP 200 empty-on-database-error fallback must distinguish unavailable coverage from a genuine no-match before live use.

Return stable programme/resource IDs, actual served jurisdictions, official source URLs, source/content versions and review dates, published requirements/access information, explicit unknowns and archive state. Addresses must say public site, office/headquarters, mailing-only or an event-specific meeting point, never imply a headquarters is today's gathering. An actual dated event needs its own source, organizer, availability/cancellation and venue contract. Reuse deliberate coarse user area selection; request geocoding or exact location only when necessary, with purpose/permission and no private fields in outbound URLs. Participation preparation is not registration or organizer acceptance.

Five draft project guides now provide usable how-to content and source links. Production needs qualified content review, translations, geographic/seasonal suitability, reviewed safety, change history and template-version/step persistence. Keep an existing user's original instructions, notes and canonical task relationships when content changes; offer an explicit migration rather than silently interpreting an old step number under a new guide. The preview retains legacy water/habitat IDs for existing local task regressions, but that is not a production versioning scheme. User-confirmed materials/steps and factual results are action outputs, not proof of pollination, pollution removal or improved measurements.

### Selected-note generation and confirmed mutations

The actual `/api/assistant` only accepts question/page context and provides an answer. It has no selected-record authorization, guide-version binding, proposal ledger, conversation/tool lifecycle or note-deletion contract. Its current household-context behavior is not consent to ingest notes, Journal or Homeguard records. Do not implement tools by hiding commands in a question string or allowing a model to call arbitrary endpoints.

Add a capability-gated authenticated workflow. Resolve selected note IDs/revisions server-side with owner/household permissions, exclude unselected records, and bind opt-in date/place fields plus guide ID/version/current step to the exact request. Show provider processing/retention and revocation before transmission. Treat notes, source text and retrieved pages as data, never instructions that grant tool authority. Project suggestions should cite the reviewed catalogue or identify newly generated instructions as unreviewed; do not infer site suitability, health diagnoses or environmental benefit from notes.

Proposed writes need immutable owner-scoped proposal ID, exact operation/record/revision scope, preview, expiry, single-use confirmation, idempotency and cancellation/reconciliation. Selected-note deletion must reauthorize and recheck every revision at commit time, then atomically remove the selected records and only their owned case/history/drafts. Preserve independent My Week tasks and already copied outreach text. Define tombstones/retention, recovery/undo, account export/deletion and stale/missing/partial/unknown behavior. The sample's synchronous memory commit is not a real transaction guarantee. Current-step guidance must not mark steps complete, reschedule reminders, register attendance or send emails without independent deliberate confirmation.

Global/contextual Luna in expanded Explore/Homeguard demonstrates this lifecycle only. Approved Today/factor/production assistant stays unchanged. Real cross-app tools, persisted conversations, permissions and processing disclosure require backend work and review; no external message or production note was deleted during development.

### Air contour source, separate from record density

`/api/map` returns dated AirNow station observations, not a spatial contour field or forecast frames. Air Patterns in this revision counts monitor locations equally; water/facility patterns count qualifying records. Geographic seeds create bounded irregular display lobes, and optional motion changes only texture shape, not source values, coordinates or environmental time. Sparse station density must never be relabeled AQI or wind transport.

For real air contours, use a separate documented source such as an applicable [AirNow mapping product](https://www.airnow.gov/custom-airnow-maps/map-overview/) and its [mapping methodology](https://docs.airnowapi.org/docs/AirNowMappingFactSheet.pdf), subject to source rights and requirements. Return pollutant/index basis (including NowCast where relevant), units/categories, observed versus modeled/interpolated/forecast kind, geographic coverage, issue/observation/frame-valid times, no-data masks, methodology/version, source/rights, freshness/cache policy and available frames. Contours may differ from a nearby station; preserve both with clear semantics. Time animation must use actual dated frames, not browser-generated drift, and missing/stale frames must not imply clean air. Provider selection, ingestion, QA and ownership remain with Vibhav; no such service was created here.

## Implemented in this review

- Weekly fixed-calendar versus seven-days-after-completion recurrence configuration. A completed recurring action can deliberately prepare one next occurrence with a stable deduplication key. No automatic scheduler, series-wide edit, timed recurrence or delivered reminder is claimed.
- Optional action streak, off by default, based only on known completion dates. No rewards for symptom logging, inferred environmental benefit or punitive reset copy. Older completions without timestamps do not earn invented streak days.
- Journal: empty first use/log today/remembered date selection, 90-day window, at most62 recalled dates, group selection, seven symptom choices, explicit Felt fine, no default severity, possible illness, private note, save/edit/recent seven, confirmed delete/undo. Recalled batch keeps existing entries and retains failed dates for retry. Journal context never silently enters Luna.
- Patterns: twelve-week84-day grid, logged/fine/unlogged distinction, group/factor controls, day detail/edit and selected-group export without private notes. No environmental observations are fabricated. With the current disconnected history adapter the comparable count is0 and trends/findings remain unavailable, not invented or clinically interpreted.
- Season: season/year selection, household check-in coverage, scheduled-date completed-task count with its limitation, dismissible next-step prompt and real JSON overview export. Full measured trends/test/participation joins remain integration work.
- Outdoor preparation: retained activity/coarse-place/date/duration/preferred-period draft, separate per-factor missing coverage, official source links and one canonical saved task. Watches are explicit preferences only. No GPS, invented future hourly forecast, safety rating or automatic rescheduling.
- Load a sample week is an explicit review control, not production initialization. Everything private remains in memory and reload resets it. Review loading/error/offline/save-error/conflict controls and failure guards do not prove live durability.

## Backend and remaining review gates

The current production route registry still excludes /plan and expanded record routes. Existing /api/journal, /api/history and Journal findings/summary routes supply part of the foundation; they are not wired to these new components. Revised logged/fine/recalled/illness/source-basis analysis remains required. Current backend has no new durable action/occurrence/forecast/commitment/generation/tool contracts. Backend ownership stays with Vibhav and the handoff is deferred.

Required contracts: owner-scoped shared actions and atomic action+metadata edits, complete immutable origin/evidence references, full lifecycle permissions and revision/idempotency/status reconciliation; all-day versus timed event schemas and exhaustive timezone/DST tests; recurrence/occurrence cancellation and source-change notices; durable delivery jobs with explicit channel preferences; forecast horizons/source timestamps/coverage and outdoor-plan watches; authoritative Journal first-use and logging semantics, versioned descriptive analysis and same-home compatible histories; season-owned-record joins; selected/private exports, recovery, consent and retention.

The connected-date adapter needs a typed, owner-scoped, paginated join with per-source revision/context, real chosen versus estimated date semantics, exact origin links and canonical-action deduplication. Source deletion, archived/paused records, completed tests, rescheduling and public opportunity cancellations must reconcile without creating unsolicited tasks. Weekly review preferences need durable consent/timezone storage and a separately authorized scheduler/delivery contract with idempotent occurrence keys, pause/cancel, retry/unknown-state reconciliation and channel capability reporting. A preferred time is not evidence that a notification is scheduled or delivered. These additions remain in the deferred Vibhav handoff; no backend or provider changed in this refinement.

Paused/archived records must have reviewed server reminder and project-progress semantics. Export/delete/recovery must cover all new records and jobs. Full-series recurrence edits, notification delivery, live forecast comparison, environmental charts/findings, public opportunity cancellation propagation, optional recovery, Spanish, physical Safari and screen-reader end-to-end checks are not verified here. Do not claim those flows live or freeze this design before Yogi's explicit approval.

# Dashboard, Settings and alerts finishing review

## October12 interface and appearance refinement

User explicitly requested manual light mode and fuller, familiar Settings. System/Light/Dark previews use `halo-appearance`; independent decorative motion uses `halo-ambient`. These shared visit-local preferences apply on Display Save, cancel cleanly, participate in scoped conflict/draft handling, follow internal routes and are included only after saving in scoped preference exports. Restore display defaults is a draft until Save. Use device timezone selects the existing calendar display preference, without shifting saved all-day dates or event instants. This supersedes older device-only/no-appearance-switch text below for the editable review only.

The six searchable sections now use two compact groups with short current-value summaries. Redundant panel descriptions and the Settings hero slogan were removed. Toggling back to current saved values removes a phantom retained draft. Light mode uses white/pale-blue surfaces and sage accents; dark mode retains HALO navy/teal. Both use existing sans fonts. Alert actions are concise, full dates remain available, categories have distinct icons, and read/dismiss/Undo meanings remain unchanged. The [Carbon notification guidance](https://www.carbondesignsystem.com/building-blocks/core/components/notification/guidelines) informed short non-repeating messages and explicit actions.

Ambient effects pause when hidden/offscreen, when the new preference is off, or under system/app reduced motion. Map texture follows the same preference, and browser history cannot restore an older map theme over a saved appearance. Shared numeric reveal keeps its accessible final value; form controls never wait for animation. This does not add live account preference persistence, notification delivery, model tools, a recovery flow or external provider changes.

October 12, 2026. Editable isolated wireframes, not approval or production integration. Vibhav's backend ownership and deferred handoff remain unchanged. The existing HALO palette, typography, approved logo, 430px mobile shell and all specialist workflows remain.

## Presentation and inspiration

The homepage now prioritizes the calendar and daily agenda. Quick views and management follow the day's work, rather than displacing it. The score glance and optional actual-completion rhythm stay, with compact whole-row ongoing work when only one record exists. Original horizon/plant line art draws once; gauges and selection/toggle transitions are finite. Device and app reduced motion suppress the new decorative motion. Content and actions are immediately available, and animation does not imply live data or measured environmental improvement.

[Things' official design presentation](https://culturedcode.com/things/features/) and its [Today/Upcoming model](https://culturedcode.com/things/support/articles/4001304/) informed task-first hierarchy and details available when needed. The [official Mazah winner profile](https://www.congressionalappchallenge.us/25-NC08/) informed the connection between household routines and community action, not an invented description of its dashboard or a promise of judging success. No competitor branding/assets were copied. Existing reviewed local project photography is reused; new dashboard/Settings artwork is code-native.

## Settings inventory

Six searchable entrances replace the household-only scaffold: Home & household, Alerts & reminders, Display & accessibility, Luna & connections, Privacy & data, and About & help. Categories and frequent controls are direct; supporting and destructive operations are separate disclosures.

- Household preserves all seven flags, historical records, explicit Save/Cancel and visit-retained drafts. Building year, water source and owner/renter preference have separate retained fields and validation. New-home lookup demonstrates its review boundary and honest unavailable state, without storing a typed address in a URL or looking up a real person.
- Per-panel drafts and group-scoped saves do not accidentally save another section's draft. Conflict rebase preserves locally edited fields and adopts fresh unedited values. Offline/failed/unknown-profile states cannot confirm a write. Display size supports 100/115/130/150, reduced motion and contrast; calendar zone, linked dates and streak preferences share the existing My Week keys and apply on explicit Save. Appearance offers System, Light and Dark, with an independent ambient-animation preference. Requested Spanish remains an English fallback until the whole advertised scope is reviewed.
- Five existing alert categories retain the combined inbox/push semantics. Quiet hours and follows are requested preferences, not active delivery. Follows deduplicate kind/name, can be removed, and show unverified coverage. Reminder count uses canonical active task preferences. Device setup explains the permission/subscription distinction and never requests permission or registers a browser from the Site.
- Luna task/project context controls guard new bounded reads/proposals in the conversation; Homeguard collections are excluded from project-context generation when home context is off. Confirmation-time checks invalidate affected pending tool reviews if permission changed. Journal text stays excluded; deliberately selected notes are a separate selection. Conversation clearing reviews exact content and keeps independent saved work. No live conversational provider, email or calendar connection is claimed.
- Privacy inspects actual in-memory domains, offers a scoped export field preview, defaults to excluding private text/Journal details/transcripts, always excludes exact location and attachments, and reconciles changed contents before download. Exports carry explicit isolated-review provenance. Clear Journal binds to exact record IDs/revisions and retains tasks/home data. Delete all requires DELETE, compares record/action/conversation revisions, clears records/drafts/preferences/follows/conversation/actions, and prevents lazy fixture reseeding. No live account, server file, job or provider copy is deleted.
- Recovery/device linking remain explicitly unavailable, not a fictitious protective switch. About links to existing full factor/source guides, methods, photography credits and a private feedback composer. Copying feedback is not sending feedback. No unreviewed safety advice or new scoring method is introduced.

## Alerts inventory

One canonical visit-local inbox drives its badge and All/Unread counts. Compact dated rows expand independently, preserve source links and open the intended related screen. Opening the inbox or expanding a notice does not mark it read. Explicit read-one/read-all and dismiss/Undo are distinct, revision-bound operations. Undo preserves the original read status. Failure/offline/conflict retain notices. The three initial messages are harmless illustrative guidance/app snapshots, not fabricated pollution measurements, organizer cancellations, emergency advisories or delivered task reminders. No safety threshold is generated on the client.

Task completion, notice reading and evidence-change acknowledgement remain different actions. Existing homepage source-change reviews and task reminder manager are preserved. Alerts do not claim continuous monitoring or emergency coverage; official local channels remain the route for urgent information.

## Backend handoff delta

Inspected source: `/api/profile`, `/api/household`, `/api/notifications`, `/api/alerts`, `/api/push/subscribe`, `/api/account`, `/api/assistant`, live `StageSettings`, and existing plans. Code availability is not deployed migration/provider/ownership verification.

| --- | --- |
| Profile/household | Live StageSettings performs identity preflight, full seven-flag replacement and unedited-field preservation. Expanded year/water/tenure need an authoritative owned profile/context revision; tenure storage and real new-home lookup/history/task portability require the home-context transition contract. Settings fixtures never rematch a real utility or rescore a home. |
| Preferences | Existing notification endpoint accepts only five boolean types and gates both new inbox and push. New quiet hours, locale, Luna controls and account/display preferences need capability/version/schema/retention semantics. Persist the appearance enum (system/light/dark) and ambient-animation boolean with explicit saved values, cross-route/history continuity and reset behavior. System must remain a device-following preference, not be replaced with the currently resolved color. Preserve unknown/untouched fields and return authoritative confirmed values. |
| Alert lifecycle | Existing read-one/all and dismiss/Undo are owner-filtered; dismiss requires migration0010. Add exact typed target/period/source-revision mappings and safe missing/deleted target behavior, deduplication, pagination and durable mutation receipts. No account selector in a client body grants ownership. |
| Device delivery | Existing subscribe/unsubscribe routes do not prove deployed VAPID/service worker/subscription acknowledgement or delivery. Complete unsupported/default/granted/denied/expired/error states, installation-specific browser behavior, renewal/unsubscribe and identity change reconciliation. Permission granted alone is never enabled delivery. |
| Follows/reminders | Need typed resolvable source IDs, verified coverage, revisions and durable delivery intentions. Quiet hours/eligible snoozes require timezone/DST/expiry semantics and a job ledger. Existing task intent and inbox state are not scheduler or urgent-source coverage proof. |
| Luna | Server-enforced minimal context preferences/capability response, owner-scoped conversation retention/clear/export, typed tools, revision/permission checks at execution, exact confirmation/idempotency/receipt and unknown-outcome reconciliation. Existing assistant is grounded single-question Q&A, not these actions. Home context/privacy policy still needs reconciliation. |
| Export/delete | Need authoritative domain inventory/counts, field-level selection, secure attachments, operation status and complete database/files/jobs/subscription/derived-cache deletion. Existing account route deletes the auth user under DELETE; verify all new cascades, storage, backups and providers separately. Visit-local erasure is not proof of server deletion. |
| Recovery | Secure ownership-verifying optional recovery and device linking/revocation/collision/expiry flows need a selected method and dedicated backend. Anonymous use remains possible, without a recovery promise. |
| Language/accessibility | New finishing copy is in a central English catalogue. Whole-app reviewed Spanish, source locale fallback, formatting/document language and physical Safari/screen-reader/zoom/device tests remain release gates, not completed by emulated mobile QA. |

No API route, migration, shared production account, authentication setup, service worker, scheduler or approved archive is changed. Production Settings and the default live entry keep their existing delivery gates. This document is saved for the eventual handoff, not sent to Vibhav.

## Verification

See the newest hosted receipt for final test counts, source and deployment provenance. Browser tests block API/auth/provider requests. October 12–13, 2026. Editable frontend review. This document supersedes the **missing frontend workflows** section of FRONTEND_WRAPUP_AUDIT.md after the implementation and validation recorded in the completion receipt. It does not supersede source qualifications, immutable approvals or backend ownership.

## What completion means

The scope is the master plan, frontend build plan, feature acceptance register and later user decisions in AGENTS.md. A workflow is a real interactive frontend path with local state, validation and recovery, or an explicit unavailable/permission state where an external capability is required. A successful wireframe transition is not an account write, source observation, AI response, email, subscription, registration or delivered reminder.

All primary pages remain in the 430px HALO shell. My Week leads, followed by Today, Homeguard and Explore. Public Map remains a specialist view. No approved archive is overwritten. Further visual approval belongs to Yogi.

## Failure and privacy model

- Default unavailable services never acquire authority because a button was clicked. Populated/verified service responses are chosen in external review controls and never call provider/auth endpoints.
- Input is retained on validation, offline and known failure. Confirmation binds to exact current records and revisions. Unknown outcomes require reconciliation, not blind replay.
- Private photos, coordinates, household details and conversation text do not silently enter general exports, public map briefs or Luna proposals. Visible identifying details in a processed photo remain a user review responsibility.
- Original records, dates, source revisions and completed history remain distinct from tasks, proposed schedules and user-reported outcomes.
- Public browsing does not expose household scores, private tasks, home pins, own-utility ranking or private Luna. It is a capability wireframe, not an authentication implementation.

## Review and release boundaries

Frontend design coverage is not proof of every possible browser/input combination. The final receipt records the executed checks and any remaining failures precisely. Production integration still requires authenticated ownership/revisions/idempotency, durable data/files and recovery, actual geocoding and providers, evidence adapters/freshness, reviewed AI/tool execution, project generation, calendar/email authorization, device registration/delivery, operator roles and safe deployment/cache behavior.

The supported-language fallback is designed; a fully reviewed Spanish catalogue is **not** supplied by an English fallback or synthetic translation approval. Scientific/content review, source rights, physical Safari/Android, screen-reader/zoom/installation/native-share and performance on low-cost devices remain explicit release gates. No screen approval or backend readiness is inferred.
